transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because I can’t seem to get past these thoughts at work, mostly. Like if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign in a system, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. And I know that sounds dramatic—part of me knows it’s not always rational—but it feels like it’s on me personally.

I manage computer systems, so there are always permissions and alerts and all that, and it’s like… I’ll try to move on, but my brain won’t let it go. I keep thinking, what if that one thing I overlooked is the thing that ruins someone’s life? Sorry, I know I’m rambling. That’s basically why I came in.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking settings over and over, or mentally going through scenarios—to try to reduce the anxiety these thoughts bring up?

Yeah… yes. I do. It’s not just once or twice, either. I’ll reread deployment plans and audit logs over and over, and then I’ll tell myself, okay, one more pass, just to be sure. But then that turns into another one.

And it’s weird because it’s not only work stuff. I’ll check door locks too, or go back through old messages, like maybe I missed something important or said something that could cause a problem. Sometimes I count through steps in my head—like a sequence has to line up right before it feels… I don’t know, safe, I guess.

I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves doing that. And I’ll know I should stop, I’ll be hungry or exhausted, but if I try to leave before it feels complete, I get this panic feeling, like I’m walking away from something dangerous.
Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that feel foreign to you—like they don’t belong—even if you know they’re not rational?

Yeah… I do. They feel like they just sort of drop into my head and then won’t leave. Like, I’ll be trying to do something normal at work, and suddenly it’s, what if I missed one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, and because of that somebody gets hurt or loses everything.

And I know—at least part of me knows—that’s not always rational. I mean, systems have layers, teams have procedures, it’s not like one thought in my head controls the universe. But it still hits me like it’s my fault already, like I’m personally responsible if I don’t catch it. Then I can’t just move on.

Sorry, I’m probably circling back to the work thing again, but that’s the main way it shows up. It doesn’t feel like a thought I chose. It feels like it barges in and demands I treat it like an emergency.
